messages:
maria: Quick check — PR #7123 (allocator + kv-cache tweak) is green on unit tests but perf CI shows a p95 tail bump for long-seq 8k runs. Planning to merge in the 11:00 UTC window unless we get objections. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7123

jordan: which benchmark specifically? I can look now.

maria: perf-run long-seq-8k on canary-3. Pattern: p50 unchanged, p95 up ~40ms, p99 up ~120ms. Throughput stable. Full CI log: https://ci.redwood/bench/longseq/2099998765

akshat: pinging in case the allocator change introduced extra KV cache invalidation on long prefix chains. Do you have the bench output?

maria: pasted the relevant excerpt below:
```
Benchmark: long-seq-8k (1000 iters)
Before (main): p50=12.4ms, p95=38.6ms, p99=102.1ms, tps=480
PR #7123:       p50=12.6ms, p95=79.1ms, p99=223.4ms, tps=472
Diff: p95 +40.5ms (+105%), p99 +121.3ms (+119%)
Heap delta: +38MB peak RSS on canary instances
```

samir: thanks. That p99 jump is significant. Can we reproduce locally with the same seed/fixture? I can run the microbench with --trace-kv to see where time is spent.

dev-ci-bot: perf job completed for commit abc123 (PR #7123) — artifacts: /artifacts/longseq/2099998765 — status: unstable (regression detected) :warning:

jordan: looking at flamegraph quickly — the extra time seems to come from cache-eviction path and a synchronization point in allocator_free_batch(); spike aligns with longer prefix chains hitting memtrim.

akshat: hmm, my change added a small refcount reorder that reduced fragmentation but might serialize frees. I'll dig in. If it's the refcount path we can gate it behind a runtime flag.

maria: proposal: hold merge, add runtime flag "alloc_no_sync_on_free" default false, run canary with flag=true to measure. If that fixes tail we'll land flag=false then iterate on safe fix. Any objections?

jordan: sounds reasonable. Two asks: 1) can we get a quick canary with 3x long-seq runs to reduce noise, 2) add a short note in PR description about the perf regression and revert plan so on-call sees it.

samir: I'll run the canary benchmark in us-west-2 with trace enabled; ETA ~25m.

akshat: I'll open a tiny follow-up PR that introduces the runtime flag and a test; will link it here.

maria: thanks — holding merge. If the canary with flag=true shows p95/p99 within 5% of main and no mem bump, we'll merge both PRs together. Otherwise we'll revert the allocator change and file a follow-up for safer approach.

dev-ci-bot: canary run started: canary-flag-test-2099998765 (nodes=4)

samir: canary run finished. Quick numbers: with flag=true -> p50=12.5ms, p95=40.1ms, p99=105.3ms, tps=478, heap delta +6MB. Looks within noise. Full traces uploaded: /artifacts/canary-flag-2099998765

jordan: verified flamegraphs — eviction hot path absent when flag enabled. LGTM from my side for merging the flag PR + original PR together once akshat's follow-up is up.

akshat: opened PR #7124 (runtime flag + test) and linked it to #7123.

maria: great. I'll wait for 2 approvals (jordan + samir) and then merge both in the 12:30 UTC window. Leaving a note for on-call: if latency regressions appear post-merge revert plan is to rollback to main and re-run canary.

samir: approving both now.

jordan: approving both.

maria: merged PRs and kicked off post-merge canary validation. Thanks everyone. Will monitor dashboards for 30m and post any alerts here. :thumbsup:

dev-ci-bot: post-merge validation started for deploy abc123 -> canary group.

maria: (later) no regressions observed in 30m window, closing the loop and marking the change as "perf-validated" in the PR.

maria: summary for release notes: resolved p95/p99 long-seq tail regression introduced by allocator reorder; temporary runtime flag added and disabled by default, safe merge validated on canary.
